full_text_en:
Hong Kong China Resources Textile Raw Materials Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Zhanjiang Shipping Agency Company, Zhanjiang Textile Enterprise (Group) Company, and Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Import & Export Trade (Group) Company — dispute over delivery and taking delivery of goods without original bills of lading

Plaintiff: Hong Kong China Resources Textile Raw Materials Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Sun Dequan, General Manager

Agent ad litem: Wang Qiming, Deputy Manager of Natural Fiber Department, China Resources Textile Raw Materials Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Ma Xiaohu, Lawyer, China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd.

Defendant: Guangdong Zhanjiang Shipping Agency Company

Legal Representative: Lin Xing, Manager

Agent ad litem: Liang Shan, Lawyer, Guangdong Commercial & Financial Law Firm

Defendant: Zhanjiang Textile Enterprise (Group) Company

Legal Representative: Lin Feiza, General Manager

Agent ad litem: Zhao Fang, Pang Baining, Lawyers, Zhanjiang No. 1 Law Firm

Defendant: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Import & Export Trade (Group) Company

Legal Representative: Zhang Shuzhi, Chairman of the Board

Agent ad litem: Zhang Guoxin, Lawyer, Shenzhen Donghai Law Firm

Agent ad litem: Liang Minghui, Staff, Shenzhen Yida Industrial Company

The plaintiff, Hong Kong China Resources Textile Raw Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Textile Raw Materials Company), brought a lawsuit before the Guangzhou Maritime Court against the defendants, Guangdong Zhanjiang Shipping Agency Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhanjiang Shipping Agency) and Zhanjiang Textile Enterprise (Group) Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhanjiang Textile Company), concerning a dispute over the delivery and taking delivery of goods without original bills of lading. After accepting the case, the Guangzhou Maritime Court held that Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Import & Export Trade (Group) Company (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Company) had a legal interest in the outcome of the case and must participate in the proceedings jointly. Pursuant to Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Court notified Shenzhen Company to join the proceedings as a defendant.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On May 27, 1989, the plaintiff entered into a contract with Shenzhen Company under which the plaintiff agreed to supply 1,908 tons of Sudanese cotton to Shenzhen Company. On July 24, upon Shenzhen Company's application, the Shenzhen Branch of the Bank of China issued a letter of credit for 945 tons of Sudanese cotton. The plaintiff chartered a vessel to transport 5,023 bales, weighing 963,583 kg, of Sudanese cotton from Port Sudan to Zhanjiang Port. The carrier issued Bill of Lading No. ZHAN/1. Zhanjiang Shipping Agency was the carrier's agent at Zhanjiang Port. Because Shenzhen Company refused to pay the purchase price, on March 1, 1991, the Hong Kong Branch of the Bank of China returned to the plaintiff the full set of negotiating documents under the letter of credit, including the original bill of lading, and the plaintiff thereby became the lawful owner and holder of the bill of lading. In May of the same year, when the plaintiff presented the original bill of lading to Zhanjiang Shipping Agency to take delivery of the goods, it was informed that the goods under Bill of Lading No. ZHAN/1 had already been taken delivery of by Zhanjiang Textile Company against a letter of indemnity. The conduct of Zhanjiang Shipping Agency and Zhanjiang Textile Company constituted an infringement of the plaintiff's ownership rights over the goods covered by the bill of lading. The plaintiff requested the Court to order Zhanjiang Shipping Agency to deliver the Sudanese cotton under the bill of lading to the plaintiff or to pay compensation of US$1,530,596.10 plus interest for losses, and to hold Zhanjiang Textile Company jointly and severally liable.

Defendant Zhanjiang Shipping Agency's Defense: The defendant, having received a valid letter of indemnity and a copy of the bill of lading from Zhanjiang Textile Company, delivered the goods in accordance with normal practice. All liability arising therefrom should be borne by the defendant Zhanjiang Textile Company.

Defendant Zhanjiang Textile Company's Defense: The plaintiff, after prolonged negotiations with Shenzhen Company and receipt of partial payment from Shenzhen Company, no longer has the right to assert any claim over the goods. Zhanjiang Textile Company merely assisted Shenzhen Company in taking delivery of the goods and was not the party taking delivery.

Defendant Shenzhen Company's Defense: Within the scope of the bill of lading dispute, Shenzhen Company has no interest in the case with the parties. The plaintiff, by avoiding the facts of its contractual dispute with Shenzhen Company and filing suit based on a bill of lading dispute, is circumventing the law. The Court is requested to dismiss the plaintiff's action.

Facts Found by the Guangzhou Maritime Court:

On May 6, 1989, the plaintiff entered into a sale contract with NORSUD S.A., Geneva, Switzerland, to purchase 1,905 tons of Sudanese raw cotton, payable by letter of credit. On May 27, the plaintiff entered into a cotton purchase contract with Shenzhen Company, agreeing to supply 1,908 tons of Sudanese raw cotton in two deliveries. On June 28, Shenzhen Company entered into a cotton processing contract with Zhanjiang Textile Company, agreeing that Shenzhen Company would supply 954 tons of raw cotton on a non-valuation basis for Zhanjiang Textile Company to process into combed cotton; Shenzhen Company was responsible for customs declaration and taking delivery, and Zhanjiang Textile Company was responsible for transporting the raw cotton from the port of entry to the factory warehouse. On July 24, upon Shenzhen Company's application, the Shenzhen Branch of the Bank of China issued Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit No. LC450890756. The letter of credit specified 745 tons of Sudanese raw cotton, unit price US$0.73 per pound, CIF Zhanjiang. On October 11, the plaintiff issued a sight draft for US$1,530,596.11, together with the full set of negotiating documents including four original bills of lading, and forwarded them through the Hong Kong Branch of the Bank of China to the Shenzhen Branch of the Bank of China, requesting Shenzhen Company to pay the purchase price. According to the bill of lading, the carrier was Pacific International Lines (PTE) Ltd., the carrying vessel was "KOTA MAJU," Bill of Lading No. ZHAN/1, the shipper was Port Sudan Cotton Co., the consignee was "TO ORDER OF: PORTSUDAN COTTON CO. KHARTOUM/SUDAN FOR A/CO OF NORSUDS A. COTTON DIV., 1204 GENEVA," the port of loading was Port Sudan, the port of discharge was Zhanjiang, carrying 5,023 bales, weight 963,583 kg, of Sudanese raw cotton. NORSUD S.A. Cotton Division endorsed the bill of lading in blank. On October 14, the Shenzhen Branch of the Bank of China received the documents under the letter of credit and notified Shenzhen Company to make payment. On October 20, Shenzhen Company notified the Shenzhen Branch of the Bank of China that it refused to pay because the documents did not conform to the terms of the letter of credit. On the same day, the Shenzhen Branch of the Bank of China notified the Hong Kong Branch of the Bank of China of the refusal to pay under the letter of credit.

On October 11, 1989, the carrying vessel "KOTA MAJU" arrived at Zhanjiang Port. Zhanjiang Shipping Agency was the shipping agent appointed by the carrier. On October 18, the "KOTA MAJU" completed discharge, and the 5,023 bales of Sudanese raw cotton were stored in the port warehouse. Shenzhen Company declared the import of the Sudanese raw cotton to Zhanjiang Customs. On October 20, Shenzhen Company went through the procedures for taking delivery of the goods from Zhanjiang Shipping Agency. As it did not have the original bill of lading, Zhanjiang Textile Company issued a letter of indemnity to Zhanjiang Shipping Agency, guaranteeing to assume any liability that might arise from Shenzhen Company taking delivery of the goods against a copy of the bill of lading. Zhanjiang Shipping Agency agreed to release the goods. On October 23, Zhanjiang Textile Company went through the procedures for taking delivery of the goods from Zhanjiang Port Authority and transferred the goods from the customs-supervised port warehouse to the warehouse of the Cargo Company of Zhanjiang Port Authority. With the consent of Shenzhen Company, Zhanjiang Textile Company took delivery of 39 bales of raw cotton on November 10 and 20 for trial spinning. In January 1990, following Shenzhen Company's instructions, Zhanjiang Textile Company transported 3,031 bales of raw cotton to Sanshui County Textile Dyeing and Printing Factory, 1,011 bales to Shekou, Shenzhen, and the remaining 942 bales were handled by Shenzhen Company itself.

After Shenzhen Company refused to pay under the letter of credit, the plaintiff and Shenzhen Company negotiated via fax regarding the quality of the goods and payment. On October 25, 1989, the plaintiff stated in a fax to Shenzhen Company: "You have already taken delivery of the goods... Please instruct the bank to remit the payment by T/T." Shenzhen Company, citing that the quality of the goods did not meet the contractual requirements, demanded compensation from the plaintiff for losses. On January 3, 1990, accompanied by Shenzhen Company staff Zhou Gangliang, Luo Yongsheng, Xu Zhaoyang, and Zhanjiang Textile Company staff Chen Ruijing, the plaintiff's employee Yu Dun went to the warehouse of the Cargo Company of Zhanjiang Port Authority to inspect the quality and storage conditions of the goods and discovered that 39 bales of raw cotton had already been removed from the warehouse. On June 11, Shenzhen Company drafted a payment agreement and notified the plaintiff: "Now, through negotiation between both parties, Party A (Shenzhen Company) will first pay US$600,000 of the purchase price; the remaining amount will be settled through negotiation between the parties based on Party A's losses." The plaintiff replied: "Now, through negotiation between both parties, Party A (Shenzhen Company) agrees to first pay US$600,000 of the purchase price; the remaining amount will be paid separately in the near future." The plaintiff and Shenzhen Company reached agreement on the advance payment of US$600,000 and the method of payment. On June 22, the plaintiff received a T/T payment of US$600,000 from Shenzhen Company.

In May 1991, the plaintiff inquired about the storage of the goods with Zhanjiang Shipping Agency, and Zhanjiang Shipping Agency replied that the goods under Bill of Lading No. ZHAN/1 had already been taken delivery of.

Opinion of the Court:

The facts of this case involve two interrelated legal relationships: first, the legal relationship of damage compensation arising from the delivery and taking delivery of goods without the original bill of lading in the maritime cargo transport between the plaintiff and the defendants Zhanjiang Shipping Agency, Zhanjiang Textile Company, and Shenzhen Company; second, the legal relationship of the international trade contract between the plaintiff and the defendant Shenzhen Company. Analyzing the logical sequence of the facts, at the time the goods arrived at Zhanjiang Port, the plaintiff lawfully held the bill of lading and was the owner of the goods thereunder. Zhanjiang Shipping Agency, as the carrier's agent, delivered the goods against a letter of indemnity without collecting the original bill of lading, violating international shipping practices. Shenzhen Company, without obtaining the original bill of lading, took delivery and actually controlled the goods, also violating international shipping practices. Zhanjiang Textile Company, by issuing a letter of indemnity to Zhanjiang Shipping Agency to enable Shenzhen Company to take delivery without the bill of lading, likewise violated international shipping practices. The conduct of the three defendants interacted and constituted a joint tort, infringing upon the legal status of the bill of lading as a document of title at that time. However, as the lawful holder of the bill of lading, the plaintiff, while having absolute ownership of the goods, did not assert its rights under the bill of lading against Zhanjiang Shipping Agency, Zhanjiang Textile Company, and Shenzhen Company based on the bill of lading for Shenzhen Company's act of taking delivery without paying the purchase price. Instead, as the seller under the international trade contract, the plaintiff negotiated with Shenzhen Company, the buyer under the international trade contract, regarding the quality of the goods and the payment, changed the payment method from a documentary letter of credit to a bank telegraphic transfer, and accepted the payment of US$600,000 from Shenzhen Company in this manner. This fact shows that the plaintiff subsequently acquiesced in the tortious act of delivering the goods without the bill of lading by Zhanjiang Shipping Agency and Zhanjiang Textile Company, as well as the fact that the goods were delivered to Shenzhen Company, and also confirmed the legality of Shenzhen Company, as the buyer under the international trade contract, taking delivery of the goods. At that point, the ownership of the goods under the bill of lading in this case had been transferred to Shenzhen Company. The plaintiff's conduct should be regarded as its voluntary continuation of performance of the international trade contract with Shenzhen Company and its abandonment of the right to assert ownership over the goods based on the bill of lading. Most importantly, the negotiation between the plaintiff and Shenzhen Company to change the payment method for the goods signified that the bill of lading no longer had the effect of a document of title; the bill of lading held by the plaintiff was merely evidence of the contract of carriage and a document for the delivery of goods. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim for compensation for the purchase price and interest losses against Zhanjiang Shipping Agency, Zhanjiang Textile Company, and Shenzhen Company, based on a bill of lading that no longer had the effect of a document of title, is not supported by this Court. The dispute over the purchase price between the plaintiff and Shenzhen Company should be resolved in separate proceedings. Accordingly, on September 29, 1993, pursuant to Article 72, paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the ownership of property acquired by contract or other lawful means shall be transferred simultaneously with the delivery of the property," the Guangzhou Maritime Court rendered the following judgment:

Judgment:

The claims of the plaintiff, Hong Kong China Resources Textile Raw Materials Co., Ltd., are dismissed.

The court acceptance fee of US$9,600 shall be borne by the plaintiff.

After the pronouncement of the judgment at first instance, neither the plaintiff nor the defendants filed an appeal.
